extracted.intended_audience: department chairs, senior researchers (nominators), and prospective early-career nominee faculty
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for nominating and evaluating candidates for the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Research Fellowship — focused on early-career, tenure-track researchers across listed scientific fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are selected on the basis of: Their independent research accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators emphasize the candidate's record of independent, significant research rather than work done primarily under another investigator. Nominated candidates are normally several years past the completion of their Ph.D. to accumulate a competitive record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are selected on the basis of: Their creativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on originality and imaginative approach to scientific problems; examples or evidence of creative independent work strengthen the nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to become leaders in the scientific community
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are selected on the basis of: Their potential to become leaders in the scientific community through their contributions to their field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee looks for indicators of future leadership — e.g., trajectory of impact, independence, recognition by peers, and the likelihood of continued significant contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process — independent committee review
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are reviewed and candidates selected by an independent selection committee of distinguished scientists in each eligible field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are made by field-specific panels of senior scientists; nominations should be prepared with the understanding that peer evaluators in the candidate's field will make the final selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — tenure-track appointment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be tenure-track, though untenured, as of September 15 of the nomination year
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold a tenure-track faculty position on the specified cutoff date; untenured tenure-track faculty are eligible, while non–tenure-track positions are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — doctoral degree and eligible fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in: Chemistry; Computer Science; Earth System Science; Economics; Mathematics; Neuroscience; Physics; Or a related field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates trained in closely related disciplines may be eligible; nominators should ensure the candidate's field aligns with one of the eligible fields or is clearly related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated candidates are normally several years past the completion of their Ph.D. in order to accumulate a competitive record of independent, significant research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship targets early-career researchers who have begun to establish independence; very recent Ph.D. graduates are typically not competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination requirement — letter of nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate must have a letter of nomination from a department head or other senior researcher
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nominating letter should come from an appropriately senior endorsing official (e.g., department chair or senior researcher) and presumably address the selection criteria (independence, creativity, leadership potential).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination limit per department
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than three candidates may be nominated from any one department per fellowship field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments should prioritize and limit nominations to a maximum of three per eligible field; coordinating internal selection or ranking processes may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award terms and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship amount: $75,000; Two-year term; Begins on September 15th of the award year
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful nominees receive a $75,000 award payable over a two-year fellowship period starting on September 15 of the award year; nominators and nominees should plan timelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation strongly encourages the nomination of qualified women, Black, Indigenous, and Latina/o/e candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators are explicitly encouraged to consider and nominate qualified candidates from these underrepresented groups to promote diversity among fellows.
